cases.sentence: Я ___ себя виноватым считал, а теперь рассудил, что это не так.
cases.explain: «третьего дня» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “In the first place, don’t dare to suppose,” she began, “that I am going to apologize. Nonsense! You were entirely to blame.” The prince remained silent. “Were you to blame, or not?”

cases.explain: «злобных мальчишках» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Oh, very well, let’s sit down, at all events, for I don’t intend to stand up all day. And remember, if you say, one word about ‘mischievous urchins,’ I shall go away and break with you altogether. Now then, did you, or did you not, send a letter to Aglaya, a couple of months or so ago, about Easter-tide?”

cases.sentence: Я просижу и проговорю с тобой десять минут; я пришла к тебе справку сделать (а ты думал и бог знает что?), и если ты хоть одним словом заикнешься про ___, я встаю и ухожу, и уже совсем с тобой разрываю.

cases.sentence: — резко спросила Лизавета Прокофьевна, выслушав письмо с ___.
cases.explain: «необыкновенным вниманием» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “My goodness, what utter twaddle, and what may all this nonsense have signified, pray? If it had any meaning at all!” said Mrs. Epanchin, cuttingly, after having listened with great attention.

cases.sentence: Там у меня бывали минуты полной жизни и ___.
cases.explain: «чрезвычайных надежд» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “I really don’t absolutely know myself; I know my feeling was very sincere. I had moments at that time full of life and hope.” “What sort of hope?”

cases.sentence: Но вот зачем я с таким нетерпением ждала тебя: я все еще верю, что ___ тебя мне как друга и как родного брата прислал.
cases.explain: «сам бог» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I have waited for you with the greatest impatience (not that you were worth it). Every night I have drenched my pillow with tears, not for you, my friend, not for you, don’t flatter yourself! I have my own grief, always the same, always the same. But I’ll tell you why I have been awaiting you so impatiently, because I believe that Providence itself sent you to be a friend and a brother to me. I haven’t a friend in the world except Princess Bielokonski, and she is growing as stupid as a sheep from old age. Now then, tell me, yes or no? Do you know why she called out from her carriage the other night?”

cases.sentence: — ___, что я тут не участвовал и ничего не знаю!
cases.explain: «Честное слово» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I give you my word of honour that I had nothing to do with the matter and know nothing about it.”

cases.sentence: Теперь и у меня ___ об этом, но еще вчера, утром, во всем винила Евгения Павлыча.
cases.explain: «другие мысли» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Very well, I believe you. I have my own ideas about it. Up to yesterday morning I thought it was really Evgenie Pavlovitch who was to blame; now I cannot help agreeing with the others. But why he was made such a fool of I cannot understand. However, he is not going to marry Aglaya, I can tell you that. He may be a very excellent fellow, but—so it shall be. I was not at all sure of accepting him before, but now I have quite made up my mind that I won’t have him. ‘Put me in my coffin first and then into my grave, and then you may marry my daughter to whomsoever you please,’ so I said to the general this very morning. You see how I trust you, my boy.”

cases.sentence: Все они теперь у меня такие, даже эта ___, Александра, но эта уж из рук вон выскочила.
cases.explain: «мокрая курица» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Nor do I believe it, in spite of the proofs. The girl is self-willed and fantastic, and insane! She’s wicked, wicked! I’ll repeat it for a thousand years that she’s wicked; they all are, just now, all my daughters, even that ‘wet hen’ Alexandra. And yet I don’t believe it. Because I don’t choose to believe it, perhaps; but I don’t. Why haven’t you been?” she turned on the prince suddenly. “Why didn’t you come near us all these three days, eh?”

cases.sentence: "___, я, конечно, не имею ни малейшего права, в глазах людей, иметь самолюбие.
cases.explain: «Милостивый государь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Sir, “In the eyes of the world I am sure that I have no cause for pride or self-esteem. I am much too insignificant for that. But what may be so to other men’s eyes is not so to yours. I am convinced that you are better than other people. Doktorenko disagrees with me, but I am content to differ from him on this point. I will never accept one single copeck from you, but you have helped my mother, and I am bound to be grateful to you for that, however weak it may seem. At any rate, I have changed my opinion about you, and I think right to inform you of the fact; but I also suppose that there can be no further intercourse between us.

cases.sentence: — Чему? ___! точно даже и не мужчина!

cases.translation: “Don’t be a simpleton. You behave just as though you weren’t a man at all. Come on! I shall see, now, with my own eyes. I shall see all.”
